generation.prompt:
Use case: photorealistic-natural. Asset type: base rock image for an interactive bouldering guide. Create an original, very ordinary candid field photograph of the described Red Rock Canyon sandstone boulder. This is a new camera composition derived solely from general factual landform descriptions, no input photo and no imitation of a specific photographer. Landscape roughly 4:3, high resolution. Rock face occupies about 85% of frame, complete base and lip visible, small natural margins. Eye-level hiker's compact-camera view, close and nearly frontal with enough perspective to distinguish edges. Modest midday desert light, realistic shadows, honest natural color and slightly uneven exposure, real granular sandstone with random weathering and fissures. A little rocky sandy desert ground at bottom and incidental distant scrub and neighboring sandstone at sides, narrow unremarkable sky margin. No humans, no gear, no lettering, no logos, no chalk route patterns, no colored marks, no route artwork, no arrows, no graphic treatment. Avoid epic scenic composition, wide landscapes, dramatic sunset, glowing rock, immaculate symmetrical boulders, smooth CGI surfaces, vector graphics, poster illustration, staged hero photography.
Subject: the south/front face of Super Scream Boulder. A low broad rectangular salmon sandstone block with a near-vertical roughly trapezoidal south face, noticeably asymmetric: a lower ledge section on the left and a taller broad flat-topped main block on the right. A prominent dark open vertical crack/cleft separates the left ledge section from the broad main face. The main face has varied shallow pockets, rough small slots and sidepull-like natural breaks, a few darker varnish patches; its right outer arete drops almost straight into a shadowed gap beside a neighboring rock. The face sits on a broken rocky foot with a small dark recess, the lower left edge steps down. The left section has a clean left outer arete. This is the front south face, so do not turn the view to the smoother overhanging east traverse wall. New near-frontal standing hiker-camera view with slightly shifted position, complete base and both top rims visible, sandstone slope just incidental behind.
